walkthroughs.body_html: Kind of Blue, recorded in two sessions (2 March and 22 April 1959) at Columbia's 30th Street Studio, remains jazz's best-selling LP. The sextet included Coltrane, Adderley, Evans, Chambers, Cobb.
So What uses two chords — D minor 7 (16 bars), Eb minor 7 (8 bars), back to Dm7 (8) — over which soloists improvise in D Dorian and Eb Dorian. Form is melodic, not harmonic.
Chord-scale theory assigns a scale to each chord: D-7 → Dorian, G7 → Mixolydian, etc. Modal jazz freed soloists from chord-change density.

mcqs.q: How does D Dorian differ from D minor?
options: It is always C major.
They are the same scale.
Dorian has a raised 6th (B natural) compared to natural minor.
Dorian has no sharps or flats at all.

mcqs.q: How do you identify a major key from its key signature?
options: It is always C major.
The number of sharps or flats equals the tonic note number.
The last sharp is the leading note (semitone below tonic); the second-to-last flat is the tonic.
Dorian has no sharps or flats at all.

mcqs.q: How does a harmonic minor scale differ from a natural minor?
options: It is always C major.
All notes are raised by a semitone.
The seventh degree is raised by a semitone (creating a leading note).
It has only five notes.
